params.body:
Three gaps in what the platform counted, each of which made a number say less than it seemed, plus one block on the Activity tab that puts the channels side by side.

## 1. A lead says where it came from (R P1-3.14)

`leads` had no origin, and all three doors (the widget's question form, the public API, the public proposal page) go through `LeadService::open`, so "which channel brings questions" had no answer.

- New nullable column `leads.source` (additive migration). Vocabulary as constants on `Lead`: `widget`, `public_api`, `proposal` (`Lead::SOURCES`). I found no other caller of `LeadService::open`.
- The source is a required **parameter** of `LeadService::open`, not a key in `$data`, so a caller cannot forget it. An unknown value still opens the lead (a customer's question outweighs our bookkeeping), stores null and is reported.
- Existing rows stay null: unknown, not guessed.

## 2. Views on a dealer's own website are counted as `site` (R P3-16.21)

StockCars renders its car pages from `GET /api/v1/public/vehicles/{id}`, and `RecordVehicleView` only ran in the `web` group, so those views were never counted.

- The same middleware now sits on that one API route, mapped to the new side `VehicleViews::SITE`. Same rules as the other sides: only a GET with 200 counts (a car outside the dealer's scope is a 404 and does not), the list and facets do not count, and the owner of the car is the garage on the row.
- **A counting failure never breaks the response**: besides the existing swallow in `VehicleViews::record`, the middleware now wraps all its counting in a try/catch, because a partner's website renders from this response.
- On this route the caller is the website's server, so its user agent says nothing about the visitor. A site that forwards its visitor's agent in `X-Visitor-User-Agent` gets its crawlers skipped like the widget's; without the header the server's own agent is judged (for StockCars that is `node`, so crawler visits to stockcars.be count until the site sends the header; follow-up in stockcars-website).
- Dated: the new measure `cars_site` and the channel take their start from the first `site` row, so the Activity screen shows "since 30/09/26" and never compares against a period that was not measured.
- To the dealer, `site` is his own website: the per-car line "x on your website, y on the platform" (R S2-5.27) adds widget and site together.

## 3. The owner's own view is not a platform view (R P3-16.22)

`ownvehicle.edit` (and `stocklist.index.detail` by the owner) counted as a platform view while only the owner's dealer was stored, so a dealer opening his own fiches inflated his own "platform" number.

**Choice: record it apart as `own` instead of dropping it.** `vehicle_views` already keys on `(date, vehicle_id, source)`, so a fourth value costs no schema change, and it gives the change a date from the data itself, the way every other counter here dates itself (`MIN(date)`): `VehicleViews::since(PLATFORM)` is the later of the first platform day and the first `own` day. That is exactly the deploy day on production (dealers open their own cars within minutes), with no hard-coded date that could drift from when the merge actually lands. `own` is outside `VehicleViews::SOURCES`: it is in no measure, no total, no per-car count and not in `since()` without a side. The decision "is the viewer the owner" is made inside the same `INSERT ... SELECT` that already reads the owner from `vehicles`, so it costs no extra query.

Result: `platform` is now the colleague (trade) view, and the measure is relabelled "Cars viewed by colleagues". `Measures::against` refuses to compare the platform measure with a window that still held the old definition.

## 4. Views per channel on the Activity tab (R P3-16.23)

A new block "Views per channel, all garages" on Inzichten > Gebruik (`Measures::channels`, rendered in `livewire/admin/activity.blade.php`), with the window options the screen already has (per month above 120 days):

- **Own website (public API)**: `site`
- **Website widget**: `embed`
- **Colleagues on the platform (buy-over interest)**: `platform`, now colleagues only
- **Widget opened**: `embed_views`, the denominator under the widget line
- **Buy-overs completed**: `vehicle_history` rows per day, as reference on the same axis

One strip per channel on a shared time axis rather than a stack (in a stack every layer above the first is unreadable). The three car-view channels share one scale so their heights compare; widget opens and buy-overs are other units and scale on their own. Each channel starts on the day it became valid; a step before that draws nothing (null, not zero), and a channel never counted says so. It reuses the existing groove/bar markup; the only CSS change is letting the block span the full width in the wide layout. `ABarYouCanReadANumberOffTest` now reads the series section for its one-series assertions, and additionally checks that every channel bar carries a readout.

## Known limits (not changed here)

- StockCars caches a car's detail per warm serverless instance (`detailCache` in `src/lib/stocklist.ts`), so repeat views on a warm instance do not reach the API: `site` is a lower bound.
- Platform staff opening a garage's car count as a colleague view.
- Per-car numbers still carry the owner's own opens written between 27 September and this deploy; they age out of the 30-day window by themselves.

## Rules

New: R P1-3.14, R P3-16.21, R P3-16.22, R P3-16.23. Updated: R P3-16.17 (the third side and the owner exclusion), R S2-5.27 (what "your website" and "the platform" mean now).

## Tests

- `WhereAViewAndALeadCameFromTest` (new, 11 tests): an API detail view is counted as `site`; 404, list, and a forwarded crawler agent are not; a forced failure on the counter's insert leaves the API response intact; the owner's own opens go to `own` and reach no count, a colleague's go to `platform`; the platform measure is dated from the split and not compared across it; the per-channel series counts all garages per day and starts at each channel's valid-from; a never-counted channel draws nothing; the Activity tab shows a strip per channel; widget and public API leads store their source; an unknown source stores null.
- `ProposalPublicPageTest`: the proposal lead stores `proposal`.
- All new tests fail on origin/main.
- Full suite locally: 2442 tests, OK. PHPStan: no errors. Pint on the new files: passed.

Migration is additive (`leads.source` nullable); Forge runs `migrate --force` on deploy.
params.title: Track where views and leads come from, and show views per channel
